_about: Official sources for the BinaSmart banking and money knowledge pack (the second sector pack; the method is design 2026-09-16-airline-travel-design.md section 1). ops/packs/fetch-pack.js --pack banking reads this file and nothing else: it fetches each site the way `fetch` says, keeps only paths matching `allow` and not matching `deny`, waits crawlDelaySeconds between requests, and writes knowledge/banking/<slug>.md. This pack INFORMS ONLY. No account page, no login page, no transaction page and no application form is ever fetched, because Bini must never look like a way to bank. reach/checked are what was measured from this VPS on the stated date; a source we cannot reach is listed as manual with the measurement and with what its absence costs, not deleted. A source we cannot reach that somebody fetched BY HAND from a machine where it answers is `fetch: dir`: it names the folder of its harvest under /root/storage/packs/banking-manual, and `ops/packs/fetch-pack.js --pack banking --from-dir <root>` builds it from that folder's manifest.json through exactly the same extract, header and writer as a fetched site, taking the url and the date from the manifest. The harvest itself is never committed; only the documents. A dir site is still knocked on every week by the freshness job, because the day it answers from this server is the day it can stop being harvested by hand. `references` names what the repository already holds so the pack never fetches the same thing twice.

pack._amHeaders: Every ENGLISH document of this pack carries an Amharic title and an Amharic key-fact summary in its header, generated by ops/packs/am-headers.js into knowledge/banking/am-headers.json and rendered by ops/packs/fetch-pack.js. Six of the seven fetched institutions publish no Amharic page at all, so the Amharic half of the header the design asked for cannot be fetched - it is written from the page text, and every digit in it is checked against that text. The travel pack does not set this and renders exactly as it always did.
pack.disclaimerEn: Interest rates, fees, tariffs and exchange rates change, often without notice. This is the page exactly as the institution published it on the date above. Confirm with the bank before you act on any figure.
pack.disclaimerAm: የወለድ መጠን፣ የአገልግሎት ክፍያ፣ ታሪፍና የምንዛሪ ተመን ያለማስታወቂያ ይለወጣሉ። ይህ ገጽ ከላይ በተጠቀሰው ቀን ተቋሙ ባሳተመው መልኩ ነው። በማንኛውም ቁጥር ላይ ከመወሰንዎ በፊት ባንኩን ያረጋግጡ።
pack.headerAmTemplate: ይህ ገጽ {fromAm} ኦፊሴላዊ ድረ-ገጽ {langWordAm} የተወሰደ ነው። {disclaimerAm}
pack._ocrNote: A document built from OCR text says so in its own header, not only in its front matter. The National Bank wrote the rule; a machine read it off a photograph of paper, and a figure in it may be a figure the machine got wrong. {ocrPages} and {ocrQuality} are the page count and the grade the OCR run itself measured, and a pack that sets neither key adds nothing - which is how the travel pack renders byte for byte what it always did.
pack.ocrNoteEn: How this page was read: the National Bank of Ethiopia published it only as a scanned PDF with no text layer, so it was read by OCR on 2026-09-17 (Tesseract 5.4.0, 300 dpi; page images: {ocrPages}) and the transcription was graded {ocrQuality}. The wording is the National Bank's; the reading is a machine's, so check any figure against the PDF itself before you act on it.
pack.ocrNoteAm: ይህ ሰነድ ከብሔራዊ ባንክ የተገኘው በስካን (በምስል) መልክ ብቻ ስለሆነ በኦሲአር (OCR) ተነቦ ወደ ጽሑፍ ተቀይሯል፤ የገጽ ብዛት፦ {ocrPages}፤ የንባቡ ጥራት «{ocrQuality}» ተብሎ ተመዝኗል። ቃላቱ የብሔራዊ ባንክ ናቸው፤ ንባቡ ግን የማሽን ነው፤ ስለዚህ ማንኛውንም ቁጥር ከመጠቀምዎ በፊት ከዋናው ሰነድ ጋር ያመሳክሩ።
pack.headerEnTemplate: Source: {url} (official {siteName} page, {langWord}), fetched {today}. Everything below is that page as the institution wrote it — every rate, fee, limit and condition is copied, not restated. {disclaimerEn} BinaSmart is not a bank: this page is information, not advice, and nothing here opens an account, moves money or applies for anything.

sites.name: Zemen Bank
sites.robots: https://zemenbank.com/robots.txt — 200, Yoast block, `User-agent: *` with an empty `Disallow:` (everything allowed) and `Sitemap: https://zemenbank.com/sitemap_index.xml`. No Crawl-delay is published, so the pack's own 5 s is used.
sites.langNote: The only Ethiopian bank in this pack with a real Amharic locale. https://zemenbank.com/am/ pages carry genuine Amharic body text (the forex-service page extracted 2,611 characters with 1,176 Ethiopic characters on 2026-09-16), not a machine-translated menu. Amharic pages are fetched and get lang: am; English pages get lang: en. One exception, measured on 2026-09-16: /am/%e1%89%b3%e1%88%aa%e1%8d%8d (the Amharic tariff url) serves the English fee table under an Amharic breadcrumb - 277 of its 279 lines are identical to /tariff and only 166 of its 16,537 characters are Ethiopic - so it is denied. The same tariff is in the pack once, in English, as zemen-tariff.
sites.pathSlugsNote: Zemen's Amharic URLs are percent-encoded Ethiopic, which the slug rule would turn into a 200-character filename of hex. Every allowed /am/ path therefore needs an explicit, readable, ascii slug. Task 4 Step 2 generates the proposed table from the live sitemap with the decoded Amharic next to each line; a human reads it and pastes it here. The two entries above were decoded and their page titles read on 2026-09-16: `የባንክ አገልግሎት` and `የውጭ ምንዛሪ አገልግሎት`. A fetched /am/ path with no entry here makes the fetcher refuse the run.

sites.name: Dashen Bank
sites.robots: https://dashenbanksc.com/robots.txt — 200, `User-agent: *`, `Disallow: /wp-admin/`, `Allow: /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php`, `Sitemap: https://dashenbanksc.com/wp-sitemap.xml`. No Crawl-delay; the pack's own 5 s is used.
sites.langNote: No Amharic locale. A few Amharic strings appear inside the English FAQ page (441 Ethiopic characters on 2026-09-16), which is the bank quoting its own product names, not an Amharic version of the page.
sites.sitemapNote: The published index at /wp-sitemap.xml lists four sitemaps, one of which holds 1,292 news posts. This registry points straight at the page sitemap (83 URLs) so that 1,292-entry file is never downloaded and no news post can slip through a future widening of the allow list.

sites.name: Commercial Bank of Ethiopia
sites.robots: none published. https://combanketh.et/robots.txt and /sitemap.xml both answer HTTP 404 rendering the site's own Next.js app shell (47,298 bytes), so there is no robots file and no sitemap to obey. The pack's 5 s pacing is applied anyway.
sites.langNote: English, with a site-wide Amharic fraud-warning banner on every page (72 Ethiopic characters) that the boilerplate strip removes because it is on every page.
sites.why-urls: There is no sitemap and no robots.txt, and the site is a Next.js application whose product pages render their content in the browser: /products/deposit extracted 462 characters and /cbe-for-you/diaspora-accounts 461, both of which are the banner plus the menu. Crawling this host blind would be impolite and would produce empty documents. So its pages are named by hand, taken from the links on /home as they were on 2026-09-16, and most of them are expected to be reported as thin. The one page that carries real content is /misalliance/terms-and-tarrif: 31,756 characters, the bank's whole published tariff.
sites.reliabilityNote: Intermittent from this VPS: 2 of 5 probes on 2026-09-16 timed out at 25 s while 3 returned 200. The two-strike `missedAt` rule in the writer exists for exactly this, and this site is the reason the mass-loss guard matters for this pack.

sites.name: Cooperative Bank of Oromia
sites.robots: https://coopbankoromia.com.et/robots.txt — 200, `User-agent: *`, `Disallow: /wp-admin/`, `Allow: /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php`. No Crawl-delay; 6 s is used here rather than 5 because this host was the slowest of the six on 2026-09-16 (/tariff/ timed out at 30 s).
sites.langNote: The English pages are the product library. /home-amharic/ and /home-affan-oromo/ exist and are fetched; the Amharic and Afaan Oromoo material otherwise lives in the news stream, which this pack does not fetch.
sites.sitemapNote: The published index lists exchange_rate-sitemap1 through 7 — thousands of daily exchange-rate posts — plus job_listing, wpdmpro and portfolio sitemaps. None of them is fetched. Only page-sitemap.xml (249 URLs) and ufaq-sitemap.xml (18) are, because those are the two that hold the products and the answers.

sites.name: Ethiopian Capital Market Authority
sites.robots: NOT PUBLISHED OR NOT REACHABLE: https://ecma.gov.et/robots.txt timed out after 30 s from this VPS on 2026-09-16, twice, while the sitemap and the pages answered 200 in about 4 s. Because we could not read a robots file we could not be told a Crawl-delay either, so 6 s is used — more than the 5 s the airline's robots asked for, on the principle that an unread robots file is treated as the strictest one we have seen.
sites.langNote: English only. A handful of Ethiopic characters appear in the titles of PDF directives listed on /laws-regulation/; the PDFs themselves are not fetched.

sites.name: EthSwitch S.C. — the national payment switch
sites.robots: https://ethswitch.com/robots.txt — 200, `User-agent: *`, `Disallow: /wp-admin/`, `Allow: /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php`, `Sitemap: https://ethswitch.com/wp-sitemap.xml`, plus a disallow on one uploads JSON file. No Crawl-delay; 5 s is used.
sites.why: EthSwitch runs the interoperable ATM and POS network every Ethiopian bank card rides on. It is the only source in the pack that can answer why a card from one bank works — or does not work — in another bank's machine. Small on purpose: 22 page URLs, of which the news, bids and job streams are denied.

sites.name: National Bank of Ethiopia
sites.hostAliasNote: The National Bank serves the same files at both spellings. Measured on 2026-09-17: of the 1,349 rows in the harvest manifest, one PDF that this pack names in allowPdf is stored only under www.nbe.gov.et — /wp-content/uploads/2021/ONPS-04-2021.pdf, the payment-instrument-issuer directive — and it silently became no document at all until this line existed. This is an allowlist of two exact host names, not a pattern: nbe.gov.et.evil.example is still refused.
sites.langNote: The manifest's own `lang` field says `am` for any page with Ethiopic characters anywhere in it, which includes /fcpe (bilingual labels), / and /200-birr. This registry does not use it. A page's language is decided by its path, exactly as Zemen's is: /am/ is Amharic, everything else is English. A bilingual page therefore says English and carries its Amharic as the institution wrote it.
sites.why: nbe.gov.et was behind a web application firewall on 2026-09-16: every path — /, /mandates/directives/, /am/, /sitemap.xml, /wp-sitemap.xml — answered HTTP 200 with the same 1,318-byte single-page application titled `Gasha WAF`, /robots.txt timed out, and a Googlebot user agent got nothing either. The pages in this pack were therefore harvested from Ibrahim's PC on 2026-09-16/17, where the site answers, and copied to /root/storage/packs/banking-manual/nbe.gov.et (721 HTML, 564 PDF, 31 REST JSON, 1.40 GB, every file SHA256-verified). The block is intermittent, not permanent: the freshness door-knock reached nbe.gov.et from this VPS at 305,103 bytes at roughly 23:50 UTC on 2026-09-16 and again on 2026-09-17. The weekly job keeps knocking; the day it answers reliably this entry can become `fetch: sitemap`.
sites.costsUs: Far less than it did. The pack now cites the foreign-exchange directive FXD/01/2024 and its amendments, the interest-rate directive NBE/INT/13/2026, the payment-instrument-issuer rules, the financial-inclusion directives and the banking proclamations by number. What is still missing is everything the National Bank publishes only as a photograph of paper: 58 of the 105 consumer-relevant PDFs in the harvest have NO text layer at all (measured with pdftotext on 2026-09-17), including the Financial Consumer Protection directive FCP-01-2020, all five currency-management directives, the credit-reference-bureau directive and the 2025 banking proclamation 1360. Those cannot be quoted until somebody OCRs them. The daily exchange-rate table is also absent: /exchange renders it in JavaScript and the harvest caught only the 345-character note above it.
sites.workaround: Ask the National Bank to let the BinaSmart user agent through, so the weekly job can keep this current instead of waiting for the next hand harvest. The OCR half of the old workaround is DONE: the scanned directives named above were read by OCR on 2026-09-17 and are in this pack — see ocrNote. What is still outstanding is Directive SMIB/4/2026 (microinsurance agents, 27 pages, 15.7 MB), which was re-fetched past the harvester's size cap, turned out to have a real text layer and therefore is NOT in the OCR folder; it sits on the workstation only and needs copying to /root/storage before it can be added. Also still outstanding: the base Directive FXD/65/2020, whose url serves its own amendment FXD/80/2022 instead, so the base text is in no harvest at all.
sites.denyNote: Measured on 2026-09-17, not assumed. /files/ holds 304 landing pages for the regulatory documents and 303 of them extract NO text at all — the title and the category render, the PDF link is attached by JavaScript — so the pack takes the PDFs instead and the landing pages would be 303 empty documents. /bank/, /insurers/, /microfinance/, /pso/, /piipso/, /capital_goods/ and /independent-forex-bu/ are 163 licensed-institution directory cards, every one of which extracts nothing for the same reason. /governace/ and /am/governace/ are 133 biographies of board members and directors. /exchange is the daily rate table, drawn by JavaScript. /treasury-bills and /open-market-operations are 252,000 characters of auction-result tables, which is a statistic, not a rule a customer can act on.
sites.ocrNote: 99 of the entries above are documents the National Bank publishes ONLY as photographs of paper, added in Task 15c. pdftotext returns zero characters for every one of them. They were read by OCR on a workstation (Tesseract 5.4.0, 300 dpi, psm 6, tessdata_best amh) and the text sits beside the PDFs at /root/storage/packs/banking-manual/nbe.gov.et/ocr/ with an ocr-manifest.json; ops/packs/fetch-pack.js reads that sidecar and never runs OCR itself. The OCR run produced 156 files of which 16 are byte-identical duplicate uploads, leaving 140; 39 of those are the insurance, reinsurance, microfinance and capital-goods-leasing series this registry has always excluded, and two more were removed by hand after being read: Limits-of-Birr-holding.pdf IS Directive FXD/49/2017, which the pack already holds from its own text layer as nbe-fxd-49-2017 (the previous report listed it as missing on the strength of its file name alone), and fis-01-2016.pdf is FIS-01-2016.pdf uploaded a second time in a different spelling with 56 fewer characters of text. THREE traps, each found by reading the document rather than its name: fxd-65-2020.pdf contains Directive No. FXD/80/2022 - the National Bank serves the amendment at the base directive's url, so FXD/65/2020 itself is in no harvest and must not be cited from this file; CMD-298-2023.pdf contains a directive that numbers itself ከማዳ 3/2015 in the Ethiopian calendar; and NBE-INT-12-17.pdf opens with the covering letter, not the rate table. All three are named in pdfTitles below. One transcript is graded poor and kept, flagged, rather than deleted: cmd-03-2013.pdf, a single bilingual letterhead page whose English letterhead came out in Ethiopic glyphs while its Amharic body and its numbering line did not - a flawed transcript of a directive is still better than a photograph, and the document says so in its own header.
sites.allowPdfNote: The one place in this registry where every entry is named rather than matched by pattern. 564 PDFs were harvested; 105 of them are about a question a bank customer asks (foreign exchange, payment instruments and mobile money, financial inclusion and consumer education, interest rates, currency, credit reference and movable collateral, the banking proclamations) and the insurance, reinsurance, microfinance licensing, capital-goods-leasing, annual-report, quarterly-bulletin and macroeconomic-statistics series are not. Of those 105, pdftotext on 2026-09-17 got usable text out of 47 and NOTHING out of 58 — the National Bank publishes a great many of its older directives as photographs of paper. The 45 listed here are what is left after two more removals: the monthly interbank-rate tables (a statistic), a conference slide deck, a press release about one auction, and three files uploaded twice under two spellings. Every one of them was measured: the smallest yields 1,290 characters and the largest 285,792, capped at 60,000 by the importer.

sites.pdfTitlesNote: A PDF's title is its file name cleaned, because the National Bank's harvest manifest carries no title for any of these. Where the file name is not what the document calls itself, the document is named here from its own first page, read on 2026-09-17: the Ethiopic-numbered currency directives keep the number as the directive writes it (ከማዳ), and fxd-65-2020.pdf is titled FXD/80/2022 because that is the directive inside it. Nothing here is a summary; every one of these strings is on the first page of the document it names.
sites.pathSlugsNote: The National Bank's Amharic site and one of its Amharic PDFs have percent-encoded Ethiopic URLs, which the slug rule would turn into 200 characters of hex. Each is named here from the page's own <title> as the harvest manifest recorded it, read on 2026-09-17. /am and /fx are named for a different reason, found by running it: the slug rule treats a leading two-letter segment as a locale prefix and drops it, so BOTH of those paths came out with no name at all — /fx, the single most important page on this host, was written as nbe-.md on the first import.

sites.name: Ethio telecom — telebirr
sites.langNote: This site carries the language in a query string, not in a path: /telebirr/faq is English and /telebirr/faq?lang=am is Amharic, and they are two documents. The importer therefore keys a page by path AND query, and langOverrides matches on the query.
sites.why: www.ethiotelecom.et resolves to 196.189.90.58 and every connection from this VPS failed on 2026-09-16 — three https probes and one http probe, all returning no bytes; telebirr.et and superapp.ethiotelecom.et do not resolve at all. The telebirr pages in this pack were therefore harvested from Ibrahim's PC on 2026-09-16/17, where the site answers, and copied to /root/storage/packs/banking-manual/www.ethiotelecom.et (99 HTML, 32.7 MB, every file SHA256-verified). The harvest covers the telebirr section and the telebirr-linked financial services only; everything outside mobile money — mobile and data packages, 5G, fixed line, enterprise, news, careers, tenders — was never fetched.
sites.costsUs: Almost nothing now: the pack holds telebirr's own pricing page, its FAQ, its registration requirements, deposit, withdraw, send money, bill payment, international remittance and every telebirr-linked credit and saving product, in English and in Amharic. What it does not hold is the Tigrinya versions (deliberately dropped — this pack is English and Amharic), the telebirr app itself, and anything on the login-walled subdomains.
sites.workaround: Re-probe on every freshness run: the day www.ethiotelecom.et answers from this server is the day this entry can become `fetch: sitemap` and stop needing a hand harvest.
sites.denyNote: Tigrinya, Oromo and Somali variants are dropped: this pack is English and Amharic, and the om and so variants served English anyway. The four Ethiopic-slug rules drop pages the CMS publishes twice — one whose slug literally contains `https-www-ethiotelecom-et-`, an older Amharic FAQ (በተደጋጋሚ የተነሱ) superseded by /telebirr/faq?lang=am (በተደጋጋሚ የሚነሱ), and Ethiopic-slug copies of Bulk Payment and Donation that already exist under their English slugs. Sixteen more duplicates were caught by the importer's own same-text rule rather than by a pattern.
sites.pathSlugsNote: Every Amharic page of this site is named by hand, from the page's own Amharic <title> as the harvest manifest recorded it, read on 2026-09-17. ?lang=am is not a readable filename and neither is a percent-encoded Ethiopic slug, so the importer refuses to guess at either.

sites.name: Safaricom Ethiopia — M-PESA
sites.titleFromNote: Every one of the 24 harvested pages carries the same <title>, `M-PESA Ethiopia |`. Twenty-four documents with one title is twenty-four documents a reranker cannot tell apart, so this site's documents are titled from each page's own first heading instead — still the page's own words, never ours.
sites.why: M-PESA is not on www.safaricom.et. That host answers 200 but renders in the browser — an invented path returns the same 17 KB shell as a real one, so a soft 404 cannot be told from a page — and its 3 harvested pages hold no M-PESA content at all, which is why this entry now names m-pesa.safaricom.et instead. m-pesa.safaricom.et returned no bytes from this VPS on 2026-09-16. Its pages were harvested from Ibrahim's PC on 2026-09-16/17 and copied to /root/storage/packs/banking-manual/m-pesa.safaricom.et (24 HTML, 1 PDF, 1 tariff JSON, 1.6 MB, every file SHA256-verified).
sites.costsUs: Very little now: the pack holds M-PESA's FAQs (with the wallet and transaction limits), its terms and conditions, its KYC requirements, its agent tiers and its own fee table. What it does not hold is anything in Amharic — this site publishes none — and the daily promotions.
sites.workaround: Re-probe on every freshness run. When m-pesa.safaricom.et answers from this server the HTML half can become `fetch: sitemap`; the fee table will still need the calculator, because it is not in any page.
sites.denyNote: The allow list names this site's pages one by one rather than allowing ^/ — the site is small enough to enumerate, and an allow list of ^/ on a site with a login route is how an informing pack becomes a banking one. The Merchant-Promotion.pdf in the harvest is a marketing leaflet and is not read. Three hub pages — /business, /mpesa-agent and /contact-us — are deliberately NOT allowed, and this is the most important line in this entry. Each of them embeds the whole Frequently Asked Questions block, so the FAQ text appeared on 4 of 23 pages, which is over the 15 % share at which knowledge/index.js calls a paragraph template and strips it from every page that carries it. Measured on 2026-09-17: with those three in, /faqs.md came out at ZERO characters and the M-PESA wallet limits were in no document at all; with them out, /faqs keeps 23,633 characters including the Level-2 balance and daily limits. Their own unique copy — 2,466, 1,595 and 751 characters of hub text — is the price, and the limits are worth more than the hub copy.
sites.tariffDocNote: The fee table is NOT in any page of this site: it is produced by a Livewire component whose initial payload ships `charges: []`, and the site's own terms (clause 2.10) say the schedule is published separately. It was captured from the calculator itself during the harvest and stored as JSON with its provenance inside it. The importer turns that one file into exactly one document, mpesa-tariff.md, whose body is the bands as the calculator gave them and one sentence saying where they came from.

sites.name: Awash Bank
sites.why: DO NOT FETCH. On 2026-09-16 awashbank.com and www.awashbank.com both resolve to 67.23.252.122, which answers HTTP 200 by redirecting to https://technobros.au/blocked.html — a 363-byte page belonging to somebody else entirely. awashbank.com.et does not resolve. Whatever is on that address is not Awash Bank's website, and putting its bytes into a banking knowledge pack would be putting an unknown third party's page in Bini's mouth. This entry exists so that a later engineer who sees `awash` missing does not simply turn fetching on.
sites.costsUs: One of the largest private banks in Ethiopia is absent: no Awash tariff, account, loan or diaspora pages.
sites.workaround: Ibrahim confirms Awash Bank's current official domain from inside Ethiopia. Only a domain he confirms goes into this file.

sites.name: Bank of Abyssinia
sites.why: bankofabyssinia.com and www.bankofabyssinia.com resolve to 102.212.71.21 and every connection from this VPS failed on 2026-09-16, over https, in under half a second — a refusal rather than a timeout. bankofabyssinia.com.et and boa.com.et do not resolve. The same probe run reached Zemen, Dashen, Coop Bank, ECMA and EthSwitch without trouble, so this is that host and not this server's network.
sites.costsUs: No Abyssinia tariff, account, loan or diaspora pages.
sites.workaround: Re-probe on each freshness run; the freshness job reports a manual source that has come back.

sites.name: Hibret Bank
sites.why: hibretbank.com.et and www.hibretbank.com.et resolve to 197.156.92.18 and both probes from this VPS on 2026-09-16 returned no bytes. 197.156.x is the same Ethiopian address range as the government hosts that answer inside Ethiopia and not from Paris.
sites.costsUs: No Hibret tariff or product pages. The pack's four reachable banks are Zemen, Dashen, CBE and Coop Bank, which is a realistic subset, not the whole market.

sites.name: Ethiopian Deposit Insurance Fund
sites.why: edif.gov.et and www.edif.gov.et resolve to 213.55.96.152 and both probes timed out at 25 s on 2026-09-16. The alternative spelling edic.gov.et does not resolve at all. This is the same behaviour as the other 213.55.x government hosts in this file.
sites.costsUs: The pack cannot answer `is my money safe if my bank fails` — no coverage limit, no eligible-deposit definition, no payout procedure. That is a question customers genuinely ask, and Bini must say it does not have the figure rather than repeating a number from memory.
sites.workaround: Ibrahim or anyone in Ethiopia saves the coverage-limit page; it then becomes a curated document written by hand, with its source URL and the date it was saved.

sites.name: Financial Intelligence Service
sites.why: fis.gov.et and www.fis.gov.et resolve to 196.189.23.50 and both probes timed out at 25 s on 2026-09-16, the same behaviour as ethiotelecom.et on the neighbouring 196.189.x address.
sites.costsUs: No official AML/KYC explanation for customers: what identification a bank must ask for, why a large cash deposit is questioned, what a suspicious-transaction report is. The pack answers the practical half of this from the banks' own account-opening and FAQ pages and attributes it to those banks.

references.name: National Bank of Ethiopia, crawled
references.note: RESOLVED 2026-09-17, in the direction this note always said it would be. knowledge/web/nbe held 60 pages crawled by knowledge/crawl.js on 2026-09-15, loaded as source `web` and truncated at 20,000 characters. The curated pack now holds the same paths in full and by hand, so the rule — one or the other, never both — was applied: `nbe` was removed from knowledge/sources-am.json, the directory knowledge/web/nbe was deleted (it is gitignored and the loader reads every directory it finds, so removing the registry entry alone would not have dropped it), and the next ingest collected its chunks as orphans. The crawler will not re-create it.

references.name: Ethio telecom, crawled
references.note: RESOLVED 2026-09-17, the same way as web-nbe. knowledge/web/ethiotelecom held 40 pages crawled on 2026-09-13 and was the only telebirr material the index had. The pack now holds telebirr's own pricing, FAQ, registration, deposit, withdraw, send-money, bill-payment and remittance pages in English and Amharic, harvested 2026-09-16/17, so `ethiotelecom` was removed from knowledge/sources-am.json, knowledge/web/ethiotelecom was deleted and its chunks were orphan-collected at the next ingest.

references.name: eServices portal entries for banks and ethio telecom
references.note: knowledge/eservices/commercial-bank-of-ethiopia.md (5 services) and knowledge/eservices/ethio-telecom.md are already curated, already bilingual, generated by ops/knowledge/eservices-to-md.js on 2026-09-14. They describe what each office lets you do online, which is a different question from what a bank charges, so they complement this pack rather than overlap it. Never edited by hand and never duplicated here.

references.name: Tax and commercial statutes
references.note: knowledge/law holds the VAT proclamation 1341/2024 (English and Amharic), income tax amendment 1395/2025 (English and Amharic), income tax regulation 410/2017, tax administration 983/2016 and amendment 1434/2026, turnover tax 308/2002, stamp duty 110/1998 and 612/2008, the customs amendment 1425/2026 and the cheques and limitation material. Tax belongs to the law source and to Asmat, not to this pack. That is why tax words are OTHER_SERVICE words in assistant/banking.js: a VAT question must not be pulled into a bank tariff page.

references.name: BinaSmart's own money pages
references.note: Already indexed as source `guide` from public/*.html via GUIDE_SLUGS in knowledge/index.js: open-bank-account-ethiopia, vat-registration-ethiopia, ethiopia-income-tax-calculator, pay-utility-bills-ethiopia, customs-import-duty-ethiopia; and as source `page` via PAGE_SLUGS: diaspora. The banking PREFER list in assistant/banking.js names these alongside the pack so a money question sees both BinaSmart's own explanation and the bank's own page. Crawling our own site would put it in the index twice. Separately: public/cbe-birr-guide.html exists and is in NEITHER slug list, so it is indexed by nothing — flagged for Ibrahim in the report, not changed by this plan.
